kept.excerpt: Israeli warplanes and artillery struck several areas of southern Lebanon early on Aug. 21, while Israeli forces carried out detonations in border towns, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) reported. Jets hit Mansouri in the Tyre district shortly after 2 a.m., with powerful explosions heard across surrounding villages and towns. Further airstrikes targeted Ali al-Taher and Dabsha hills near Nabatieh al-Fawqa, as well as the area around Kfar Roummane.
kept.relevance: Provides cutoff-day evidence of continuing Israeli air operations, with the reported impacts located in southern Lebanon rather than Greater Beirut.

kept.excerpt: The IDF says it struck a building in southern Lebanon earlier today after several suspects crossed the ceasefire line and entered it. Soldiers of the Kfir Brigade spotted the suspects crossing into the military’s buffer zone in the area of the village of Baraashit. The army says the suspects who entered the building “posed a threat to IDF troops,” and that a short while later, the Israeli Air Force struck the site.
kept.relevance: Records an attributed Israeli military account of an executed airstrike on the cutoff date, illustrating the operational trigger while identifying a location outside Greater Beirut.

kept.excerpt: Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is designating 10 individuals that are part of a network responsible for transferring cash to Hizballah. The network utilizes couriers travelling on commercial airline flights between Lebanon, Turkiye, the UAE, and Iran to move up to hundreds of millions of dollars between jurisdictions, providing an avenue outside the formal financial system for Hizballah to obtain foreign currency and evade sanctions. OFAC is also re-designating Hizballah for service to the Iranian regime under the command of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF).
kept.relevance: Supplies an official, contemporaneous account of U.S. pressure on Hezbollah’s financing and its relationship with Iran, relevant to the wider escalation backdrop.

kept.excerpt: On Sunday, the Israel Defense Forces said it had killed a senior Hezbollah commander in an airstrike in the southern Lebanon town of Deir al-Zahrani the previous day. It said the Saturday morning strike on Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din came in response to a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in the predawn hours Saturday that seriously wounded three soldiers. Hezbollah said the Israeli strikes would be met with an “appropriate” response, urging authorities to halt “humiliating” negotiations with Israel.
kept.relevance: Documents the recent attack-and-retaliation mechanism and Hezbollah’s stated response, both relevant to the risk of geographic escalation toward Beirut.

kept.excerpt: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people Saturday, in the deadliest attacks since a truce between Israel and Hezbollah went into effect on June 20. Hezbollah has refused direct talks and wasn't party to the deal.
kept.relevance: Establishes a recent escalation in strike severity despite the truce and identifies Hezbollah’s exclusion from the diplomatic agreement.

kept.excerpt: The seventh round of talks between Lebanon and Israel concluded in Rome on Thursday without a breakthrough on key territorial issues, but with agreements on procedural frameworks and prisoner lists, according to sources close to the negotiations. All the participants underscored the importance of upholding the current ceasefire and agreed to pursue a new United Nations Security Council resolution that would serve as the international framework for arrangements following the mandate of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL). The next round is tentatively scheduled for September 1.
kept.relevance: Provides the diplomatic constraints and a negotiation schedule known before the cutoff, with the next planned round falling after the August 31 resolution deadline.

kept.excerpt: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs Sunday in retaliation to a Hezbollah missile attack on northern Israel, Israeli officials said. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the strike answered Hezbollah missiles fired at northern Israel earlier Sunday, which the Israeli military says it intercepted.
kept.relevance: Provides a dated historical precedent for Israel extending retaliation into Beirut’s southern suburbs even when the triggering Hezbollah missiles were intercepted.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-08-21. Included only sources whose displayed publication or update date was on or before the cutoff; dates were verified from web_search results containing source text and date labels. Excerpts are factual source passages, with claims attributed as in the reporting. web_fetch failed because multiple fetch providers were registered; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable and no further fallback-channel attempts were made. Verification therefore relies on search-indexed source text rather than independently retrieved full pages. Later-dated search results, undated pages, retrospective timelines, prediction-market pages, prices, and resolution outcomes were excluded. Southern-Lebanon incidents and threats are included only as forecasting context, not as evidence of a qualifying Greater Beirut impact. No forecast or resolution judgment is supplied.
